items.author: Ben King, Galen Bower, Parker Case, Hannah Kolus, John Larsen, Nathan Pastorek, Nathan Wiens
items.title: Estimating the US Energy System Impacts of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act
items.summary: Rhodium modeled transmission, gas pipeline and data-center ratepayer provisions of the initial text introduced September 30 against a current-policy baseline, and reports 2040 ranges for emissions, household bills and clean-resource build.

quote.text: Taken together, these provisions uniformly reduce economywide greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by 5-148 million metric tons annually in 2040 and as much as 1.5 gigatons cumulatively, compared to without BAAJA.
quote.speaker: Rhodium Group authors, analysis note

items.author: Kevin Rennert and Aaron Bergman
items.title: Projected Effects of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act on the Power Sector
items.summary: RFF ran the power-sector provisions of BAAJA through the ReEDS model and reports emissions, electricity-system cost and transmission effects relative to a baseline.

quote.text: We project near-term emissions reductions from the power sector of roughly 200 million tonnes (Mt) of carbon dioxide, with cumulative carbon dioxide emissions from the power sector declining by about 1.8 gigatonnes (Gt) through 2041 as compared to the baseline.
quote.speaker: Kevin Rennert and Aaron Bergman, authors

items.outlet: Center for Climate and Energy Solutions (C2ES)
items.author: Greenline Insights (modeling for C2ES)
items.title: New Nationwide Analysis: Bipartisan Transmission Reforms Would Boost Clean Energy, Cut Power Sector Emissions, Lower Electricity Bills, and Strengthen Grid Reliability
items.summary: C2ES and Greenline model nationwide effects of BAAJA's transmission and interconnection provisions to 2035, and state that delay to 2030 would forgo part of the modeled benefits.

quote.text: Reduce annual power sector carbon dioxide emissions by 173 million metric tons, a 13 percent reduction relative to business as usual.
quote.speaker: C2ES release, modeling by Greenline Insights

items.outlet: The White House (Council of Economic Advisers)
items.author: Council of Economic Advisers
items.title: The Economic Benefits of Permitting Reform
items.summary: The Council of Economic Advisers estimates long-run GDP and tax-revenue effects of cutting federal review times to the levels BAAJA requires.

quote.text: We find that reducing review times down to the levels required by the BAAJA would: Increase long-run GDP by between 0.28 percent and 0.56 percent (i.e., $82 billion to $164 billion in additional output each year).
quote.speaker: Council of Economic Advisers, The White House

items.author: not stated
items.title: Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) of 2026: Analysis of Division A, Title I, Including National Environmental Policy Act Provisions
items.summary: CRS compares each NEPA provision of Division A, Title I as introduced with current law; the report gives statutory deadlines and appropriation levels, not outcome estimates.

quote.text: Section 1101 would specify that NEPA prescribes a procedure to inform the public about environmental effects of federal actions, describes the result of the NEPA process as an informational document, and does not mandate a particular outcome.
quote.speaker: Congressional Research Service report R49510

items.author: not stated
items.title: Congress Tweaks Permitting Bill, But Deal Remains Fatally Flawed
items.summary: Earthjustice says the November 7 amendment makes no substantial Clean Water Act improvements and that the bill would still limit court review of permits and projects.

quote.text: What the amendment does: The amendment makes no substantial improvements to the Clean Water Act provisions of BAAJA.
quote.speaker: Earthjustice, policy analysis

items.author: Frank Sturges
items.title: Revisions to BAAJA permitting certainty provisions fall short of addressing risks
items.summary: CATF says the November 7 manager's amendment reduces but does not eliminate risks that section 1401 poses to future greenhouse-gas and other pollution control standards.

quote.text: The manager’s amendment to BAAJA released on Saturday, November 7, makes several changes to section 1401, many of which improve the section by reducing future risks.
quote.speaker: Frank Sturges, Clean Air Task Force

items.author: Jordan Nader, Tom Opdyke
items.title: BAAJA Blast Part 2: What Does Permitting Reform Mean for the Environment?
items.summary: R Street reviews the NEPA, Clean Water Act, Endangered Species Act and permit-certainty titles that fall under the Environment and Public Works Committee, and says it has reservations but supports the bill overall.

quote.text: Ultimately, we believe that, despite our noted reservations, BAAJA as a whole is a product of serious negotiation between political parties and committees that will benefit the American people
quote.speaker: Jordan Nader and Tom Opdyke, R Street Institute

items.author: William Driscoll
items.title: Watchdog group predicts utilities will oppose transmission reform that could yield 200 GW of clean energy
items.summary: pv magazine reports American Clean Power's projection that the transmission provisions could enable about 200 GW of clean energy, and reports a watchdog's expectation that utilities will oppose them.

quote.text: ACP projects that the bill’s reforms of transmission planning and siting could enable “roughly 200 GW of clean energy, with more as the grid expands.”
quote.speaker: William Driscoll, pv magazine USA

items.author: not stated
items.title: The Faulty Logic at the Heart of Environmentalist Opposition to BAAJA
items.summary: Breakthrough argues that critics' emissions estimates rely on assumptions that drive results, cites RFF and SEIA modeling of power-sector benefits, and says more modeling shows lower emissions.

quote.text: Since these reflexive pronouncements, more modeling has been released, which shows the ways in which BAAJA’s passage is likely to lower, not raise, emissions.
quote.speaker: Breakthrough Institute, analysis

estimates.title: Estimating the US Energy System Impacts of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act
estimates.direction: Rhodium reports that the provisions reduce economywide GHG emissions compared with a no-BAAJA case; the note also says gas pipeline changes would add emissions in isolation and that the bill is not a climate bill.
estimates.scenario: 2040, compared with a current-policy baseline without BAAJA; 1.5 gigatons cumulative reduction also reported
estimates.assumptions: Models key components of the initial version introduced September 30, against a current-policy baseline. Heatmap's account of the base case says data centers make up about 17% of electricity demand by 2040.
estimates.quote: Taken together, these provisions uniformly reduce economywide greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by 5-148 million metric tons annually in 2040 and as much as 1.5 gigatons cumulatively, compared to without BAAJA.

disputed_by.who: Heatmap (reporting Rhodium's best case; figures differ from Rhodium's own note)
disputed_by.quote: economy-wide emissions by 4%, reduce energy bills by $78 per year, and drive more than 200 gigawatts of new clean energy capacity by 2040, compared to status quo policy.

estimates.title: Estimating the US Energy System Impacts of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act
estimates.direction: Household electricity bills fall, because easier permitting lets lower-cost resources connect and the bill bars charging non-data-center customers for data-center grid costs.
estimates.scenario: 2040, compared with the same world without BAAJA
estimates.assumptions: Combined impact of the modeled provisions; base case assumes data centers about 17% of electricity demand by 2040 (per Heatmap's account).
estimates.quote: We project that the combined impact of these provisions would reduce household electricity bills by $50-78 per year in 2040 compared to without BAAJA

estimates.title: Estimating the US Energy System Impacts of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act
estimates.direction: Transmission provisions raise the interregional build rate to nearly three times the last decade's average and add clean resources, per Rhodium.
estimates.scenario: Through 2040, compared with a world without BAAJA; build rate 1.9 to 2.6 terawatt-miles per year (Rhodium's range, per Heatmap)
estimates.assumptions: Transmission provisions of the initial text; 17-249 GW is the range Rhodium reports.
estimates.quote: The transmission provisions of the bill enable accelerated average interregional transmission build rates nearly triple that of the last decade or more and drive an additional 17-249 GW of clean resources to be built through 2040.

estimates.title: Estimating the US Energy System Impacts of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act
estimates.direction: The bill as a whole increases LNG export levels, on top of a 76-145% increase already under current policy.
estimates.scenario: Compared with a no-BAAJA baseline (current policy); time frame not stated in the sentence
estimates.assumptions: Rhodium says it did not account for how exports affect the energy mix or emissions in the rest of the world (per Heatmap).
estimates.quote: The bill as a whole increases liquefied natural gas (LNG) export levels by 8-15% beyond a 76-145% increase already happening under current policy.

estimates.org: Center for Climate and Energy Solutions (C2ES), with Greenline Insights
estimates.title: New Nationwide Analysis: Bipartisan Transmission Reforms Would Boost Clean Energy, Cut Power Sector Emissions, Lower Electricity Bills, and Strengthen Grid Reliability
estimates.figure: 173 million metric tons, a 13 percent reduction
estimates.direction: Annual power-sector CO2 falls relative to business as usual in 2035.
estimates.scenario: 2035, annual, relative to business as usual; contiguous US; reform scenario modelled by Greenline Insights
estimates.assumptions: Models the key BAAJA provisions on interconnection and transmission planning; the release says the reforms would enable 170 GW of added wind, solar and storage by 2035.
estimates.quote: Reduce annual power sector carbon dioxide emissions by 173 million metric tons, a 13 percent reduction relative to business as usual.

estimates.org: Center for Climate and Energy Solutions (C2ES), with Greenline Insights
estimates.title: New Nationwide Analysis: Bipartisan Transmission Reforms Would Boost Clean Energy, Cut Power Sector Emissions, Lower Electricity Bills, and Strengthen Grid Reliability
estimates.figure: 170 GW of additional wind, solar, and battery storage capacity
estimates.direction: The modeled reforms add capacity relative to business as usual, and expand interregional transmission capacity by 61 GW.
estimates.assumptions: Modeled provisions include interconnection and transmission planning; the release does not restate other assumptions in the quoted sentence.
estimates.quote: by 2035 the modeled reforms would enable 170 GW of additional wind, solar, and battery storage capacity

estimates.org: Center for Climate and Energy Solutions (C2ES), with Greenline Insights
estimates.title: New Nationwide Analysis: Bipartisan Transmission Reforms Would Boost Clean Energy, Cut Power Sector Emissions, Lower Electricity Bills, and Strengthen Grid Reliability
estimates.figure: 800 million metric tons of emissions reductions (forgone) and roughly $55 billion in electricity system savings
estimates.direction: A delay of the reforms until 2030 would forgo part of the modeled savings and emissions reductions through 2040.
estimates.scenario: Through 2040, if the reforms are delayed to 2030 (the release says a 2030 delay yields about 40 percent of 2035 benefits by 2035)
estimates.assumptions: Release says new interconnection processes and transmission projects take years to deliver.
estimates.quote: Through 2040, this delay would forgo roughly $55 billion in electricity system savings and 800 million metric tons of emissions reductions.

estimates.title: Projected Effects of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act on the Power Sector
estimates.figure: roughly 200 million tonnes (Mt) of carbon dioxide near-term; about 1.8 gigatonnes (Gt) cumulative through 2041
estimates.direction: Power-sector CO2 falls relative to baseline, with near-term cuts of about 200 Mt and cumulative cuts of about 1.8 Gt through 2041.
estimates.scenario: Central policy scenario, ReEDS model, baseline without BAAJA; near-term and cumulative through 2041
estimates.assumptions: ReEDS (90 regions, detailed transmission) run on the modeled provisions of BAAJA as introduced September 30, 2026.
estimates.quote: We project near-term emissions reductions from the power sector of roughly 200 million tonnes (Mt) of carbon dioxide, with cumulative carbon dioxide emissions from the power sector declining by about 1.8 gigatonnes (Gt) through 2041 as compared to the baseline.

disputed_by.who: Breakthrough Institute (cites RFF and SEIA modeling at different figures; does not match RFF's own 200 Mt near-term figure)
disputed_by.quote: Fresh modeling from Resources for the Future and the Solar Energy Industries Association pegs power sector emissions benefits at around 114 million and 300 million tons of CO2 reductions per year over the next decade, respectively.

estimates.title: Projected Effects of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act on the Power Sector
estimates.figure: more than $350 billion through 2050 in net-present-value terms
estimates.direction: Savings on the electricity system, with national electricity prices decreasing.
estimates.scenario: Net present value through 2050, central policy scenario versus baseline
estimates.assumptions: ReEDS modeling of BAAJA's provisions; RFF's summary does not state the discount rate in the quoted sentence.
estimates.quote: BAAJA is projected to save more than $350 billion through 2050 in net-present-value terms, decreasing national electricity prices.

estimates.title: Projected Effects of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act on the Power Sector
estimates.figure: 3.5-7.0 percent lower average annual costs of the electricity system
estimates.direction: Average annual electricity-system costs fall over the modeled period.
estimates.scenario: Over the modeled period, central policy scenario versus baseline
estimates.quote: Reduce the costs of providing electricity, decreasing the average annual costs of the electricity system by 3.5–7.0 percent over the modeled period.

estimates.title: Projected Effects of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act on the Power Sector
estimates.figure: 30 percent increase in overall transmission capacity by 2041
estimates.direction: Transmission capacity rises over the baseline, and interregional transmission capacity more than doubles.
estimates.assumptions: ReEDS, which has detailed transmission representation.
estimates.quote: By 2041, we project overall transmission capacity to increase by 30 percent over the baseline; interregional transmission capacity more than doubles.

estimates.org: Columbia Center on Global Energy Policy
estimates.title: Project timeline savings under BAAJA (interactive tool, potential time saved by project type)
estimates.figure: 64 months (up to the federal decision, transmission archetype)
estimates.direction: Under BAAJA's deadlines the replayed transmission archetype reaches the federal decision 64 months sooner than under current law.
estimates.scenario: Composite transmission archetype replayed under BAAJA's deadlines; time counted only up to the federal decision; excludes state siting and the FERC backstop permit (Sec. 2101), which the tool says account for most of the projected transmission time savings
estimates.assumptions: Replays recorded past project dates under the bill's proposed deadlines (for example 28 months from NOI to EIS, two months after final EIS for the decision). Tool counts months saved, not projects enabled. Date shown is the announcement date reported in search; the page itself shows Oct. 6, 2026 as the date its permitting-dashboard data were downloaded.
estimates.quote: which account for most of the projected time savings for the transmission archetype. Up to the federal decision, that archetype saves 64 months.

estimates.org: Council of Economic Advisers (The White House)
estimates.title: The Economic Benefits of Permitting Reform
estimates.figure: $82 billion to $164 billion in additional output each year (0.28 to 0.56 percent long-run GDP)
estimates.direction: Reducing review times to the levels BAAJA requires raises long-run GDP.
estimates.scenario: Long-run, relative to current review times; BAAJA's two-year EIS deadline
estimates.assumptions: Review times reduced to the levels BAAJA requires (the page says BAAJA would require EISs within two years); the page's other scenario (completion in one year) gives 0.41 to 0.83 percent.
estimates.quote: We find that reducing review times down to the levels required by the BAAJA would: Increase long-run GDP by between 0.28 percent and 0.56 percent (i.e., $82 billion to $164 billion in additional output each year).
